column1: # boru Language Specification: boru:fn-util behaviour rows (frontier)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# TWO refusals live here, and they are different.
# THE BEHAVIOUR ROWS def-bind a fn computed by a FnUtil word, and the
# compiled lane refuses that shape:
#     def-bound computed fn apply (closure shape unknown — Stage 1)
# — the §5.4 / NUR101 family, shared with the U-combinator and compose rows
# in frontier-hof-audit.tsv. Nothing about it is fn-util-specific: the
# `const` row proves it, refusing identically even though `_f_const` takes
# TAny and so was never subject to the fn-operand gate. Graduation = the
# def-bound computed-fn model.
# (Until 2026-08-25 these rows refused EARLIER, with "function-valued operand
# at <word> (Stage 3)" — the recorder's default assumption that a fn-valued
# operand means the handler re-steps it on the tape. fn-util does not: it
# stashes the fn and invokes it from a Go handler. Declaring that
# (CompileStoresFn, see lang/go/modules/fn.go) removed the first wall and
# left the real one visible. The two `curry` REFUSAL rows compiled once it
# lifted and now live in lang/spec/module-fn.tsv.)
# THE LAST TWO ROWS are not that family at all: `FnUtil.flip 5` is refused
# by the strict-lane CHECK, as [uncalled_function] "call to 'flip' matched
# no signature", before compilation is reached. Graduation = the check
# admitting a dispatch whose failure is the program's specified result.
# The interpreter is the oracle that the vocabulary WORKS.
import "boru:fn-util"  def addone x:Integer => [add 1 x] end def double x:Integer => [mul 2 x] end def h (FnUtil.compose addone/v double/v) end (h 5)
import "boru:fn-util"  def addone x:Integer => [add 1 x] end def double x:Integer => [mul 2 x] end def h (FnUtil.pipe addone/v double/v) end (h 5)
import "boru:fn-util"  def k (FnUtil.const 7) end (k 99)
import "boru:fn-util"  def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] end def fs (FnUtil.flip sub2/v) end (fs 3 10)
column3: flip reverses the signature order: sub2 10 3

import "boru:fn-util"  def sq x:Integer => [mul x x] end def gt2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Boolean][a gt b]] end def bigger (FnUtil.on gt2/v sq/v) end (bigger 5 3)
